endorsements.quote: If your software influences a clinical decision, UK Medical Device Regulations (UK MDR 2002) apply.
If borderline, document the rationale and seek MHRA borderline advice early to avoid reclassification late in procurement.
Research studies or un-marked device investigations need MHRA “no-objection” and HRA/REC clearance via IRAS.
Data should reflect: (i) the target population, (ii) the intended clinical setting and workflow, and (iii) technical quality (e.g., imaging acquisition quality and device/software heterogeneity).

Subgroup performance report : demonstrate and transparently report performance for each group , not only overall averages; treat any clinically meaningful disparity as a patient-safety risk that requires mitigation actions and governance sign-off.

Dataset documentation (“health dataset factsheet”) written in plain language that states the dataset’s origin and purpose, sampling strategy, aggregation decisions (including any changes to demographic coding), missingness and measurement validity, and known/expected data shifts over time (population, practice, devices, software).
Pre-specified contextualised groups of interest relevant to the use case (not limited to one protected characteristic; allow intersectionality and local context).
External validation plan using datasets/systems not used during development (e.g., other Trusts/regions/vendors) to evidence generalisability to routine NHS practice.

Drift surveillance plan : specify what will be monitored over time (input quality, case-mix, outcome rates, performance metrics), thresholds for investigation, and actions (recalibration, retraining, rollback).
Consult the ‘STANDING Together consensus recommendations’ and use CONSORT-AI/DECIDE-AI/TRIPOD+AI where applicable to make bias and generalisability claims auditable by reviewers and adopters.
Every release—no matter how small—needs a mini risk-assessment and an update to the safety file.

unlisted_practices: Classify software as a medical device accurately and avoid under-classifying its risk class.
Write an intended-purpose statement including only claims that can be substantiated, and treat it as a controlled document that triggers review when changed.
Generate evidence aligned with NICE methods from the outset, including recruiting representative populations, patient-relevant outcomes, and sufficient follow-up.
Complete a DPIA and document lawful bases, applying data protection by design, and prototype with anonymous or synthetic data where possible.
Meet the Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC) during procurement.
Push software updates promptly when safety signals emerge.
Publish validation evidence continuously to build credibility.
Secure milestone-linked funding early for multi-year AI validation.

screen.reason: The paper is an implementation-focused guide/roadmap offering recommendations and framework steps for deploying AI in the NHS, illustrated via a descriptive case study of AI stroke imaging decision-support software.
